summary.headline: Scoda Tubes FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR518.7 crore and PAT 22% to INR38.8 crore, while Q4 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore after a March gas shutdown.
summary.overview: FY26 was a transition year with revenue up 7% to INR518.7 crore, EBITDA of INR76.2 crore and margin down to 14.7% from 16.1%. Q4 FY26 revenue was flat at INR123.6 crore, EBITDA margin 13.5% and PAT down 7% YoY to INR6.3 crore, as a 15-17 day PNG gas-driven plant shutdown in March cut production by about 40% for the month. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 25% with 14-15% EBITDA margin, backed by a 8,000 MTPA welded expansion (INR40 crore) on top of the 13,000 MTPA welded line funded from IPO proceeds. Capex was INR110 crore in FY26 and about INR100 crore is planned for FY27.

financial_highlights.value: around INR175 crore, executable in 3-4 months

segments.name: Seamless (piercing mill)
segments.commentary: Seamless capacity raised to 20,000 MTPA, total capacity 21,000 MTPA in FY26; piercing plant was shut for about 15-17 days in March on gas shortage and resumed in April. Seamless utilisation expected around 70% in FY27 and optimum in FY28.

segments.name: Welded
segments.commentary: New welded facility targeted to be operational in H2 FY27 with trial runs by end-Q2 FY27; 13,000 MTPA line funded from IPO, plus 8,000 MTPA (INR40 crore) from internal accruals, taking welded capacity to 21,150 MTPA by H1 FY28. Welded utilisation expected around 25% in FY27; optimum FY29.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue)
segments.commentary: India INR339 crore, Europe INR137.8 crore, Americas INR30.7 crore, others INR8.9 crore. Management cited domestic INR344 crore and export INR174 crore on the analyst's summation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 25%, with domestic about 20% and export about 25%; management called this conservative and will revisit in H1 FY27.
Target FY27 revenue mix of roughly 40% export and 60% domestic.
Inventory days expected to fall from 217 days to about 160 days in FY27 and remain 160-170 days thereafter.
Peak debt expected to rise by about INR50 crore to about INR250 crore in FY27; debt to decline once new capacity is fully utilised.
No further equity dilution planned; new capacity funded by internal accruals and term loans. No new seamless capex planned; further capex decision deferred to FY29-FY30 based on market conditions.
Solar project (8.79 MWdc: 4.99 MW seamless, 3.8 MW welded) expected to generate about 137 lakh kWh a year and save about INR8-8.63 crore a year in power cost.
Power and fuel cost about 17% of total expenses; gas prices up about 25%, to be passed through to customers.
Management said operations are fully normalised for Q1 FY27 with a higher cost base, and the plant is running at full capacity.
capex_capacity: Seamless capacity 20,000 MTPA, total 21,000 MTPA as of FY26 after additional lines and equipment.

Welded: 13,000 MTPA from IPO proceeds (capex INR45 crore, still underway); equipment from China expected July-August 2026 after delay from geopolitical and logistics issues; trial runs targeted end-Q2 FY27.

Additional 8,000 MTPA welded (INR40 crore, internal accruals and term loans) expected around Q1 FY28; total welded 21,150 MTPA by H1 FY28; optimum utilisation FY29. Welded range extended to 16 inches.
IPO proceeds of INR220 crore: about INR27 crore spent on capex and INR50 crore on working capital; about INR74.2 crore remaining in bank.
FY27 capex planned at about INR100 crore. Mother hollow mill supplies 70% captive consumption, targeting full captive by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material is stainless steel round bar made from imported scrap; base-material prices up 25-30% due to the war. Management said these are passed through to customers at order booking or dispatch.
LPG and gas prices remain elevated; cost pressure passed to customers with a lag. Management said demand is intact and only pricing is affected.
Export end-use: about 50% oil and gas, the rest engineering, automotive, power, and cooling industries. Europe pending Rina marine approval for Italian market, expected within 3-4 weeks.

Domestic power demand hinges on a BHEL tender now expected June-July 2026 (earlier slipped from Nov-Dec 2025 and Mar-Apr 2026); Scoda is BHEL- and NTPC-approved and works with BARC. Power sector demand is for seamless tubes.
Data centre, HVAC, cooling and water-treatment demand targeted through welded pipes; no data-centre order book yet, with inquiries on hand and orders expected around Q4 FY27.
Receivable days rose sharply (receivables up 36% vs revenue up 7%), attributed to industry-wide supply chain disruption and longer payment cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the high-diameter welded pipe capex delayed from Q3 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed geopolitical shortages, higher logistics and energy costs, and container and shipping constraints for machines from China. Delivery now expected July-August, against a prior plan of Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 weakness and was it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March gas shutdown (about 15-17 days, roughly 7-8 March to 21-22 March) was the largest headwind; without it, Q4 revenue could have been about INR140 crore. Demand is intact, and gas availability has normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the planned acquisition withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited cross-border remittance, regulatory, banking and forex constraints, plus the EU safeguard duty rising from 25% to 50% and a tariff-rate quota cut of 50% from 1 July, which removed the benefit of a European entity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for FY27 guidance and domestic/export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is conservative: domestic about 20% and export about 25% growth, with the mix targeted at 40% export and 60% domestic. Upside is seen from a BHEL win and data-centre welded demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the shift from 8-inch to 16-inch welded pipe made?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers in data centre, HVAC, cooling and water-treatment packages prefer one supplier covering up to 16 inches, so Scoda extended its welded range beyond 8 inches. Above 16 inches needs a different A358 technology.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise despite lower borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to borrowings for ongoing capex, the solar project and higher working-capital use, plus interest on delayed income tax payments.

risks_watch: Gas and LPG cost inflation and supply continuity; a repeat of March-type shutdown would hit volumes again.
Raw material (imported scrap-based stainless round bar) volatility, with a 25-30% rise to be passed through on order booking; lag risk on margins.
Delays in welded equipment delivery (July-August) could push welded commissioning beyond H2 FY27.
Receivable days and inventory days (217 days, target 160-170) affect working capital and debt, with peak debt near INR250 crore.
Order book of INR175 crore covers only 3-4 months; large export and BHEL tender timing (June-July) is uncertain.
Management withheld volumes, utilisation by segment, realisation per ton, EBITDA per ton and order-book split, limiting transparency.
Q4 FY26 PAT fell 7% and the company says the Q4 margin was hit by under-absorbed fixed costs; benchmarking against peer margins was declined.
Management agreed to consider quarterly calls and disclosure of new orders, as requested by an analyst, with no commitment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term growth story and on normalisation, but cautious and at times evasive on specifics: pricing, volumes, realisations, order-book split and peer comparison were withheld citing competitive reasons. Guidance is described as conservative and subject to review in H1 FY27 given geopolitical uncertainty.
key_quotes: Coming to FY27, we are expecting a 25% revenue growth with 14% to 15% EBITDA margins.
So, for now, we don't have any plan for diluting any more equity.
Yes, sir. Everything is smooth now. Everything is normalized, just a little bit higher cost.
